transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Since my husband passed, it feels like everything inside me just shut down, and I can’t make myself do the things I used to care about. It is just so hard to find the strength to do anything anymore.

Did these feelings start soon after your husband passed and stay mainly tied to that loss, or have they become a more constant depression affecting most of your day regardless of reminders? How long has this been going on?

They started in the year after my husband passed, but it has become a constant, numb way of living that goes far beyond normal grief. This shut-down feeling has stayed about the same for a little over two years now.

Have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others say isn’t true? Also, have you had any thoughts of wanting to die or kill yourself?

Most days, especially in the evenings, I hear my husband's voice plain as day calling my name or telling me not to trust people at the door, and it scares me so much that I just freeze. But no, I have never had any thoughts of wanting to die or hurt myself.

When you hear your husband’s voice, is it mostly about guilt, worthlessness, death, or other themes that fit with feeling deeply depressed? Or does it mainly involve things like people trying to harm you or warnings unrelated to your mood?

No, he doesn't say things about guilt or feeling worthless at all. He mostly calls my name from the back bedroom or the garden, and he warns me not to trust the people who come to the door. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the doorbell.

When you hear your husband’s voice or feel unable to trust people at the door, does that happen only when you’re feeling especially depressed, or does it also happen even when your mood is not as low? Before your husband died, had you ever had similar experiences or beliefs?

No, I never had any experiences like this before my husband passed away; it all started after he died. Hearing his voice and feeling so scared has been happening pretty regularly over the last few months, and it doesn't just happen when I'm feeling at my lowest or grieving intensely.

Over the past two years, have you also had persistent symptoms of major depression most days—like feeling sad or empty, losing interest in almost everything, changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, poor concentration, or strong guilt/worthlessness? Or have the main problem been the voice and mistrust without those depressive symptoms being present most of the time?

The shut-down feeling, having no energy, and completely losing interest in things I used to love like my quilting and choir have been there almost every day for over two years. However, hearing my husband's voice and getting frozen or pacing around only started happening regularly over the last few months.

During the last few months when you’ve been hearing your husband’s voice, have there been any stretches of at least 2 weeks when the voice and mistrust were present even though your depression was not as bad or had briefly lifted? Or do the voice and mistrust only happen during times when the depression is clearly severe?

No, that heavy, shut-down feeling has been completely constant and hasn't lifted or gotten better at all over these past two years. The voices and mistrust started a few months ago right alongside that numbness, so there has never been a time when the depression cleared up while the voices kept happening.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent major depressive syndrome with anhedonia, low energy, and pervasive depressed/numb mood, along with auditory hallucinations and suspiciousness. The psychotic symptoms occur only in the context of ongoing severe depression and there is no period of psychosis outside the mood episode. The hallucination content is not mood-congruent, but psychotic depression can include mood-incongruent features; among the provided options, severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms is the best fit.
